import { Steps, Aside, Tabs, TabItem, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import SeqDiagram from '../../../components/SeqDiagram.astro';

This tutorial walks one path from nothing to a running key-value app on the
component SDK (`calimero-app-sdk`): you write a small Rust crate, test it on the
real engine, build it into a `calimero:app` component, create a context from it,
and call its methods, checking the output at each step.

The worked example is the in-repo [`apps/kv-store`](/build/examples/#kv-store)
app, trimmed to the parts you need the first time through.

<Aside type="note">
  The Rust code, the build command and the `meroctl` flags here are taken from
  `apps/kv-store/`, `crates/app-build` and the CLI definitions
  (`crates/meroctl/src/cli/`). Calimero is pre-1.0, so flags can still change:
  run `meroctl <command> --help` to confirm them for your build.
</Aside>

## 1. Prerequisites

<Steps>

1. **Rust with the `wasm32-wasip2` target:**

   ```sh
   rustup target add wasm32-wasip2
   ```

2. **A running cluster.** You need `merod` up and `meroctl` signed in to it. For a
   local development node: `merod local` in one terminal, then
   `meroctl node add local http://127.0.0.1:2501/ --allow-mock` and
   `meroctl login --dev-passkey ./dev-passkey.json --name ada`. See
   [Run local nodes](/contribute/development/#run-local-nodes).

</Steps>

## 2. Create the project

A component app is a standalone `cdylib` crate that depends on the SDK and
nothing else from Calimero:

```toml
[package]
name = "kv-store"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[lib]
crate-type = ["cdylib"]

[dependencies]
calimero-app-sdk = { git = "https://github.com/calimero-network/core", tag = "<sdk-tag>" }

# The test harness (TestApp) and the builder, for `cargo test` on the host.
[target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dev-dependencies]
calimero-app-sdk = { git = "https://github.com/calimero-network/core", tag = "<sdk-tag>", features = ["testing"] }
calimero-app-build = { git = "https://github.com/calimero-network/core", tag = "<sdk-tag>" }
serde_json = "1"

# Its own workspace root.
[workspace]
```

Every module starts from one import:

```rust
use calimero_app_sdk::prelude::*;
```

## 3. Define the state

State is a struct of handles annotated with `#[app::state]`; loading it reads
nothing, and each field names its own keys in the app's storage. Records live in
a `Table`, declared with `#[derive(Record)]` and a `#[table]` attribute naming the
key (and any indexes, unique constraints and counts):

```rust
#[derive(Record)]
#[table(key = "key")]
pub struct Entry {
    pub key: String,
    pub value: String,
}

#[app::state(version = 1)]
pub struct KvStore {
    entries: Table<Entry>,
    size: Counter,
}
```

The app runs on its cluster's leader, which orders every write in the app's log,
so a later `set` of a key replaces an earlier one; there is nothing to merge.

## 4. Add logic, events and errors

<Steps>

1. Declare the events and errors inside the `#[app::logic]` module, where the
   ABI picks them up:

   ```rust
   #[app::event]
   pub enum Event {
       Inserted { key: String, value: String },
       Updated { key: String, value: String },
   }

   #[app::error]
   pub enum Error {
       NotFound { key: String },
   }
   ```

2. Add the logic block. Every app has one `#[app::init]`; a `&mut self` method is
   a call, a `#[app::view]` reads:

   ```rust
   #[app::logic]
   impl KvStore {
       #[app::init]
       pub fn init() -> app::Result<Self> {
           Ok(Self::load())
       }

       pub fn set(&mut self, key: String, value: String) -> app::Result<()> {
           let event = if self.entries.contains(&key)? {
               Event::Updated { key: key.clone(), value: value.clone() }
           } else {
               self.size.add(1)?;
               Event::Inserted { key: key.clone(), value: value.clone() }
           };
           self.entries.upsert(Entry { key, value })?;
           env::emit(event, Audience::All)?;
           Ok(())
       }

       #[app::view]
       pub fn get(&self, key: String) -> app::Result<Option<String>> {
           Ok(self.entries.get(&key)?.map(|e| e.value))
       }

       #[app::view]
       pub fn get_result(&self, key: String) -> app::Result<String> {
           match self.entries.get(&key)? {
               Some(e) => Ok(e.value),
               None => Err(Error::NotFound { key }.into()),
           }
       }
   }
   ```

   A few things to notice:

   - Method and argument names reach the ABI in camelCase: `get_result` is
     `getResult`.
   - `env::emit` sends an `#[app::event]` value to an audience (`All`, the caller,
     an org, a team, named accounts).
   - An `#[app::error]` variant reaches the client as `422 APP_ERROR` with
     `{ "code": "NotFound", "fields": { "key": ".." } }`.
   - `u64` and `i64` arguments and results travel as decimal strings.

</Steps>

## 5. Test it

`calimero_app_sdk::testing::TestApp` runs the built component on the real engine
in an org you describe, as named accounts, with the node's own checks:

```rust
use calimero_app_build::build_component;
use calimero_app_sdk::testing::{Org, TestApp};
use serde_json::json;

#[test]
fn set_then_get() {
    let dir = std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"));
    let target = std::path::PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR")).join("guest");
    let component = build_component(dir, &target).unwrap().component;
    let mut t = TestApp::new(&component, Org::new().members(["bob"]), 1_700_000_000_000);

    t.as_("bob").call("set", json!({ "key": "k", "value": "v" })).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(t.as_("owner").view("get", json!({ "key": "k" })).unwrap(), json!("v"));
    assert_eq!(t.events_for("owner")[0].0, "Inserted");
}
```

The same steps can live in a scenario file, `scenarios/<name>.json`, which
`calimero_app_sdk::testing::run_scenario` runs in the harness and the cluster
runner runs on real nodes (see [Testing](/build/testing/)):

```json
[
  { "as": "bob", "op": "call", "method": "set", "args": { "key": "k", "value": "v" } },
  { "as": "owner", "op": "view", "method": "get", "args": { "key": "k" }, "expect": { "ok": "v" } },
  { "as": "owner", "op": "view", "method": "getResult", "args": { "key": "x" },
    "expect": { "error": "NotFound", "fields": { "key": "x" } } }
]
```

Run both with `cargo test`.

## 6. Build and run

Build the component (from a checkout of core, or with the `mero-app-build`
binary):

```sh
cargo run -p calimero-app-build -- path/to/kv-store --out kv_store.wasm
```

It compiles the crate for `wasm32-wasip2` and lifts the ABI into the
component's `calimero:abi` section, which the node reads.

<Steps>

1. **Create a context** from it. On a development cluster `--path` uploads a raw
   `.wasm` (a signed `.mpk` installs a package):

   ```sh
   meroctl context create --name my-kv --path kv_store.wasm --alias my-kv
   ```

2. **Call the setter.** A call without `--view` is an intent the leader logs:

   ```sh
   meroctl call -c my-kv set --args '{"key": "hello", "value": "world"}'
   ```

3. **Read it back** with a view:

   ```sh
   meroctl call -c my-kv get --args '{"key": "hello"}' --view
   ```

   The answer carries `"world"` and a receipt signed by the answering node.

</Steps>

## 7. Make it multi-user

Create the context in an organization and invite someone to it:

<Steps>

1. Create the organization and the context in it:

   ```sh
   meroctl namespace create team
   meroctl context create --name team-kv --path kv_store.wasm --namespace <org-id> --alias team-kv
   ```

2. Invite a second account and have it join:

   ```sh
   meroctl namespace invite <org-id> --role member      # prints a token
   meroctl namespace join <token>                       # signed in as the other account
   ```

3. Write as one account and read as the other:

   ```sh
   meroctl call -c team-kv set --args '{"key": "from", "value": "bob"}'
   meroctl call -c team-kv get --args '{"key": "from"}' --view
   ```

</Steps>

Every replica applies the same log, so a read on any node that has applied the
write sees it.
